chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad from Hariz from one who informed him from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When you are in the obligatory prayer and you see a slave of yours who has run away, or a debtor who owes you money, or a snake that you fear for your life, then break the prayer and follow the slave or the debtor, and kill the snake."

key_terms.غَرِيماً لَكَ عَلَيْهِ مَالٌ: A debtor who owes you money
key_terms.غُلاَماً قَدْ أَبَقَ: A slave who has run away

ai.seo_question: What are the valid reasons for breaking the obligatory prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that specific worldly necessities—such as pursuing a runaway slave, recovering debt, or eliminating a feared snake—constitute valid excuses for breaking the obligatory prayer. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of balancing spiritual devotion with practical preservation of property and safety, distinguishing these immediate concerns from mere distractions.
